newsitem.title: UK: UK Nov PMI index 54.4 pct, prices index 42.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK Nov PMI index 54.4 pct, prices index 42.3 pct.

text.p: The UK Purchasing Managers' Index slipped to a seasonally adjusted 54.4 percent in November from 54.5 in October but still reflected expansion in the manufacturing sector for the sixth consecutive month, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
It said the driving forces behind the latest expansion were the continued strong growth in output and a further acceleration in the rate of growth of new orders.
"The improvement in order books occurred in spite of the recent rise in the sterling exchange rate," the CIPS said.
A reading of the PMI below 50.0 indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining; above 50.0, that it is generally expanding.
Sterling rose by around 10 percent between August and November on a trade weighted basis, dampening overseas demand for some UK goods, the CIPS said.

Export orders continued to grow, but the strengthening of sterling was reported to have reduced some sales, especially for components. "But greater demand for goods in the domestic market more than made up for any export losses."
The CIPS said the appreciation in sterling also had a downward impact on prices paid for inputs, which fell for the thirteenth month in a row in November.

Average input prices fell to a greater extent than in the previous month. "This represents a turnaround from the findings between August and October, when the rate at which prices were falling was found to have steadily eased," the CIPS said.
"The recent increase in deflationary pressures was almost entirely a result of the stronger pound making imported inputs cheaper in sterling terms."
The availability of inputs generally remained good, although just under 10 percent of firms saw delivery times lengthen as suppliers incurred delays in meeting order levels.
Order levels for consumer goods again showed the sharpest rise, prompting producers of these goods to further boost output and employment.
This rise was offset by slightly slower growth in the production of non-consumer goods, which the CIPS said was in part a reflection of uncertainty about future business conditions.
"This uncertaity was also reflected in employment, which rose only modestly in November," it said.
Following is a table of seasonally adjusted PMI indices (previously reported October figures in brackets):
NOVEMBER OCTOBER
Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) 54.4 54.5 (54.5)
Quantity of Purchases 54.8 53.2 (52.8)
Suppliers' Delivery Times 47.9 48.1 (48.1)
Stocks of Purchases 43.6 42.6 (42.7)
Stocks of Finished Goods 46.4 44.9 (44.9)
Employment 51.4 52.6 (52.6)
NOTE - the PMI is based on a weighted average of seasonally adjusted measures of output, new orders, suppliers' delivery times, stocks of items purchased and employment.
